sentences.text: Albertavenator was a small-bodied member of the troodontid theropod family.
Its frontal bone has a top surface that is relatively short, measuring less than 30% longer than it is wide.
A skull fragment discovered in 1993 at the Bleriot ferry on the Red Deer River was first thought to be a Troodon fossil.
The species Albertavenator curriei was officially named and described in 2017 by David C. Evans, Thomas M. Cullen, Derek W. Larson, and Adam Rego.
This dinosaur belongs to the family Troodontidae within the larger clade Paraves.
Researchers distinguished it from other Canadian materials and proposed removing it from Troodon, noting that the latter taxon is based on teeth.
Fossils of Albertavenator were found in the Horseshoe Canyon Formation in Alberta, Canada.
The environment where it lived was significantly cooler than other nearby geological formations.
Its time range spans from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
